outcome: Admission to intensive care due to fetal distress
cohort: The study included 240 pregnant women diagnosed with third-trimester iron deficiency anemia, along with a matched control group of non-anemic pregnant women.
finding: Third-trimester iron deficiency anemia significantly increased the rates of adverse fetal and maternal outcomes, including cesarean delivery, preterm labor, and low birth weight.
mod_finding: Anemia during pregnancy significantly increased cesarean delivery rates (70.8% vs 50% in controls) and decreased vaginal birth rates (29.2% vs 50% in controls).
